findings.description: The JSDoc (L66-69) and the ADR amendment say every metacharacter pup's matcher reads literally is refused, so that a gitignore- or bash-style matcher cannot read a stored scope wider. The check only covers `[ ] { } \`. The extglob characters `( ) | + @ !` are also escaped or literal in `globToRegExpSource` and still pass. Trigger: `pup plan edit --rescope '@(.github)/**'`, `'+(.github)/**'` or `'!(src)/**'`. There is no `*`/`?` in the first segment, no bracket or brace, and the first segment is not literally `.github`, so all three are accepted and stored. Under picomatch (extglob on by default) or bash with `shopt -s extglob`, the first two read as `.github/**` and the third as every top-level directory but `src`, `.github` and `.claude` included. That is exactly the widening the new rule claims to close. `scripts/@(pre-commit)` gets past `reachesPreCommit` the same way. pup's own matchers read all of these literally, so nothing in the tree is reachable today. This is a nit only because the threat is the same hypothetical other matcher the ADR names. Suggested fix: widen the class to `/[[\]{}\\()|+@!]/` and add the three examples to the refusal table.

`reachesPreCommit`'s JSDoc (and the ADR amendment) says the edit hooks read a bare directory glob such as `scripts` as everything beneath it, but `globToRegExpSource('scripts')` compiles to `^scripts$` and both the scope hook and `auditScope` match it literally; only a trailing `/` expands. A maintainer trusting the comment would think dropping the `dir` branch opens a hole, when it only over-refuses.

`PRE_COMMIT` hardcodes this repo's hook path (its own comment says "in a repo with no `.husky`, as this one"), but `assertRescopableGlob` runs for every project pup manages; rescopeTask resolves the task's project. Trigger: an operator of another project whose `scripts/` holds only build scripts and no `scripts/pre-commit` runs `pup plan edit --rescope 'scripts/**'` (or `scripts/*` or `scripts`). The rescope is refused with "reaches `scripts/pre-commit`, the hook that checks a worker's own commits", naming a file that does not exist there. Meanwhile a project whose hooks live elsewhere (`.githooks/`, a `core.hooksPath`, `lefthook.yml`) gets no protection. A nit because the operator can still name individual files, and the ADR accepts refusing `scripts/**`. Two ways out: have the check consult the project's `repoPath` (whether the file exists, or its `core.hooksPath`), or have the ADR state that pup-wide refusals are tuned to this repo.

The `.husky` entry (lines 94-97) and the `scripts/pre-commit` entry (lines 98-101) refuse the same thing, the git hooks that check a worker's own commits. They differ only in the path and the message. Fold them into one entry: `(_raw, form) => /^\.husky(\/|$)/i.test(form) || reachesPreCommit(form)`, with one message such as "reaches the git hooks that check a worker's own commits (`.husky`, `scripts/pre-commit`)". That removes one table row and one near-duplicate message. It also matches the existing PROTECTED entry, which covers several paths in a single row. A refusal would then name both hook paths instead of only the one hit; that is the cost.

`reachesPreCommit` has exactly one caller, the table entry at line 99, and no named second use. `PRE_COMMIT` is used only by the helper and that entry's message. It compiles `new RegExp(globToRegExpSource(form), 'i')` on every call, while `PROTECTED` precompiles its regexes once. Inline the helper into the entry and drop the named function, which also removes its separate JSDoc block (the 'any case' wording moves into the GLOB_REFUSALS doc). If a helper stays, the per-call regex can't be hoisted, because it depends on `form`. A literal path test such as `form` as a prefix of `PRE_COMMIT`, plus a match against a fixed regex, would avoid building a regex per refusal check.

The ADR 0115 amendment is dated but names no PR; docs/adr/README.md (L19-21) asks an amendment to be "dated, with the PR", as ADR 0164 does with `*Amendment (2026-11-11, #309).*`. Write `*Amendment (2026-11-13, #331): ...*`.

process_issues.description: Skipped review-context (no spec/protocol/infra surface), review-workflow-safety (no workflow change), review-maintainability (off default roster), review-spec (no closing issue or spec source).
A `git ls-files` call was refused under the CI Bash lock; the reviewer fell back to a Glob search for the file-existence check.
Injected convention rules arrived as `@docs/conventions/...` import lines with no body text; the reviewer read general.md and testing.md directly to quote them.
